page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 12 dedicated virtual CPUs and 48 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz across 6 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The CPU includes 35 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. The server contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate multi-threaded capacity paired with restrained single-core throughput. Single-core tests like stress-ng and Geekbench register in lower performance tiers, reflected in single-threaded Gzip compression at 19.02 GB/sec and Bzip3 decompression at 7.27 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded operations perform within average benchmark ranges, achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 8808.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 10042.20. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 56.47 GB/sec, while write bandwidth measures 44.31 GB/sec. In database evaluations, it processed 8.35 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance exhibits hardware trade-offs typical of legacy compute platforms, where single-threaded execution limits high-throughput single-task execution, and LLM inference drops to 6.84 tokens/sec on 7B models. Its balanced resource distribution provides qualitative cost efficiency for steady mid-tier workloads that do not demand modern clock speeds or local NVMe storage. Appropriate workloads include general microservices, multi-threaded web backend applications, micro-batch processing, and relational or key-value database execution using attached persistent disks.
